metaDescription: Kevin examines anti-gravity research and the deaths of scientists Amy Eskridge and Ning Li, alleging a suppressed technology and a possible cover-up.
summary: Kevin examines the history of anti-gravity research and its link to dead and missing scientists, starting from the Cybertruck bomber Matthew Livelsberger's warnings about anti-gravity. He reviews 1950s aerospace research by firms such as Lockheed, Boeing and Bell, then argues the work went quiet. He focuses on Amy Eskridge, whose death in 2022 was ruled suicide, and on Ning Li, whose son says she worked on classified Pentagon projects before being struck by a car. Kevin says he suspects a cover-up and names General McCasland as a central figure.
